clue.text: 13 apostle, nut at scene of vice

definitions.note: 13 points to the entry for free trade, so this means a preacher of that cause

parts.note: a cob is a hazelnut
a den, as in a den of iniquity, is a place where vice goes on

explanation.surface: A preacher of some cause, a nutcase, turns up at a den of iniquity.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Cobden was the Victorian politician who campaigned for free trade and against the Corn Laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Cobden was the leading Victorian campaigner for unrestricted commerce, so he was its apostle.

clue.text: Olympian hiding what he was, the Queen being his equal?

indicators.note: the Olympian conceals his former job inside his name

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, Olympic runner and chair of the London 2012 Games
Coe was formerly a Conservative MP, a Member of Parliament
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An Olympic champion hides his past role, the Queen being his equal.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe was MP for Falmouth before running the London 2012 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is an archaic word for a peer, an equal or companion.

clue.text: Wide girl?

explanation.definitionFit: Broad means extensive from side to side, and in US slang it is a woman.

clue.text: Possible 1 down with Roman instead of Catholic ruler

indicators.note: a possible version of the word is one of its rearrangements
one letter is put in place of another

parts.note: the answer to 1 down
R is an abbreviation for Roman

explanation.surface: A possible equal, being Roman instead of Catholic, would be a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing C to R in COMPEER gives OMPEERR, which 'Possible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme sovereign of an empire, a ruler.

clue.text: Base player playing lover of 16 down 11 in dream

definitions.meaning: the base of something is its lowest part

definitions.text: player playing lover of 16 down 11 in dream
definitions.meaning: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the weaver who plays Pyramus, lover of Thisbe, played by the bellows-mender Flute

explanation.surface: A lowly actor takes the role of a craftsman's sweetheart in a dream play.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom the weaver plays Pyramus in the mechanicals' play; Thisbe is played by Francis Flute, the bellows-mender of 16 down/11.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest part of anything is its foundation, and Shakespeare's weaver Nick plays Pyramus opposite Flute's Thisbe.

clue.text: O for publicity?

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for the element, and Margaret Thatcher spoke of denying terrorists the ... of publicity

explanation.definitionFit: The letter O stands for this gas in chemistry, and the oxygen of publicity is a famous phrase.

clue.text: Four-letter word used by Margaret raised with final twist by model

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

indicators.note: the last two letters of the name are twisted round, swapping places
in a down entry, raised means read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A four-letter word used by Margaret, held up with a twist at the end by a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the name upwards, and 'with final twist' swaps what were its last two letters, now at the front; Gervase notes a tetragram is more usually a four-sided figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetra- means four and -gram means something written, so a word of four letters.

clue.text: Mother not keeping well may need succour, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that words are said aloud, here both the wordplay and succour, heard as sucker

parts.note: mam is a northern word for mother; someone not keeping well is iller, in poorer health

explanation.surface: A mother in poor health may need help, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' also works on 'succour', heard as 'sucker', the baby who needs the nipple.
explanation.definitionFit: A mamilla is a nipple, which a sucking infant needs, and succour sounds like sucker.

clue.text: Edward West after higher education and before 19 20

indicators.note: the name follows the education

parts.note: uni, short for university, is higher education
Ted is a short form of Edward
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Edward West after university and before the next part of the saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'United we stand, divided we fall', so this half comes before 19/20.
explanation.definitionFit: The rallying cry runs: united we stand, divided we fall, so this half comes first.

clue.text: A little while after morning rounds

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, so the morning comes first

parts.note: a.m. stands for the morning hours
a mo is a moment, a little while

explanation.surface: A short time after breakfast, the doctor does the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' looks like a doctor's visits, but it means bullets or shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, and rounds are individual shots or cartridges.

clue.text: Pages about Jessica (say) and Dalyell once put on a postcard

indicators.note: the pages are placed around the other pieces

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page, and pp for pages

indicators.note: the word in brackets signals that the surname is to be taken by its sound, with a changed spelling

parts.note: Jessica Ennis, the heptathlete who won Olympic gold in 2012
Tam Dalyell, the long-serving Scottish Labour MP

explanation.surface: Someone writes about an Olympic athlete and a veteran politician on an old postcard.
explanation.walkthrough: Jessica Ennis won Olympic heptathlon gold in 2012; '(say)' admits the spelling only roughly matches her surname, as commenters grumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-penny stamp was the old postage rate stuck on postcards, so it was once put on them.

clue.text: See 16 down
Digital covers with responsibility shared between nose and tail

indicators.note: when duties are shared out between two parties they are redistributed, so the letters of the two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Coverings for fingers come with duties split between the front and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' looks like computing, but digits here are toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are digits, and the horny plates on them are their coverings.

clue.text: Geordie endorsement of raid announced in Far East's first economic community

indicators.note: the dialect word and the sound-alike go inside the word far

parts.note: taken as written
reet is the north-east England pronunciation of right, said in approval; a Geordie is someone from Tyneside

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, giving letters that sound like it

parts.note: raid spoken in a Tyneside accent sounds like rade
E is the abbreviation for East
A is first, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: A Tynesider's approval of an attack is announced in the first letter of the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far East's first' looks like it wants just the letter F, but Far stays whole as the container, and East and first each give a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A free trade area is a group of countries with no tariffs between them, an economic bloc.

clue.text: Seasonal food, say, including flower, say

indicators.note: the outer pair of letters takes in the flower and the second example

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
the aster is a daisy-like flower
again eg, for example

explanation.surface: A seasonal treat, for example, containing a flower, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate eggs are eaten at Easter, so they are a food tied to one season.

clue.text: See 13
CID purchase spring onion with diamonds inside?

indicators.note: the onion and diamonds are put inside the word for purchase

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
sybo is a Scottish word for a spring onion
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Detectives buy a spring onion with gems inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is British slang for a police detective, so the CID is cryptically a body of busies. SYBO is a Scots word for a spring onion.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy is slang for a detective, so the Criminal Investigation Department is a group of them; the usual sense is a meddler.

clue.text: Flute makes a loud noise and people return blushing

parts.note: to bellow is to roar loudly
men means people

indicators.note: the colour is read backwards

parts.note: a blushing face is red

explanation.surface: A flute player makes a loud noise and the audience come back red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Flute in A Midsummer Night's Dream is the bellows-mender, so 'Flute' is a name, not an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Francis Flute repairs the bellows used to fan fires, his trade in the Dream.

clue.text: Study lunatic among solvers off the peg

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: the madness sits inside the word for solvers

parts.note: the setter addresses the solvers as ye, old form of you
lunatic means mad

explanation.surface: A study of a madman among crossword solvers, bought off the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes off the peg are made in standard sizes ahead of sale rather than tailored.

clue.text: Notes on drink for settler

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: Musical notes on a drink for a colonist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settler' looks like a pioneer, but it is something that settles a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding game or goal is the one that settles the result.

clue.text: Rest of saying about hanging separately, with gap between backward minority and the whole

definitions.text: Rest of saying about hanging separately

parts.note: things with a gap between them are split apart

indicators.note: the word for a minority is read backwards

parts.note: a few is a small number, a minority
all means the whole

explanation.surface: The end of a proverb about hanging, with a gap between a reversed few and everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Franklin's quip was that 'we must all hang together, or assuredly we shall all hang separately', a version of this saying.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb's second half follows united we stand, and Franklin's joke about hanging restates it.

clue.text: See 19
Run away from exam with maximum speed

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: A student runs away from an exam as fast as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift, and the superlative is the quickest of all.

clue.text: Preserve eggs for graceful sculptor

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Preserve some eggs for an elegant artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Antonio Canova was an Italian neoclassical sculptor known for graceful marble figures such as The Three Graces.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Canova was the Italian neoclassical carver famed for elegant marble figures.

clue.text: Bilingual elevation of the good and generous

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevation lifts the words so they read upwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: Bilingual praise for the virtuous and open-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bilingual' signals two foreign languages: Spanish EL and French BON, turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble person is high-minded and magnanimous, giving freely.

clue.text: Tipped off about Farrow and Eden?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was warned about the actress Mia Farrow and the prime minister Anthony Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The names invite a search for MIA or AVON; they are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tipped off is to be given advance warning of something.

clue.text: See 16
Time put into underhand in a sensible way

indicators.note: the period of time goes inside the word for underhand

parts.note: sly means underhand or crafty
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Time goes into underarm bowling, done in a sensible way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage means wise, so acting wisely is acting in a sensible manner.

clue.text: One on your side at the end of the day

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday, taken here as the day at the end of the working week
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who backs you up when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' is a cliché for 'ultimately', but here the day is Friday, the end of the working week, so the clue is almost an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal or ally is someone who supports you and takes your part.
